headline: DISCOVERY MINING POSTS RECORD $319.1M Q2 REVENUE: +100% YoY, 67,309 oz Gold — Kidd Operations Adds Copper and Zinc as Cash Hits $364.3M Debt-Free
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) reported Q2 2026 record revenue of $319.1 million on gold production of 67,309 oz (+33% YoY) — more than double Q2 2025 and 12% above Q1 2026. Adjusted net earnings climbed to $92.3 million from $28.4 million a year earlier, EBITDA reached $170 million, and the company ended the quarter debt-free with $364.3 million in cash and $607.8 million total liquidity. Q2 results include one month of production from the Kidd Operations acquisition (closed June 1), adding copper and zinc output alongside critical-mineral processing capacity to what has historically been a pure gold company — a strategic pivot that mirrors the broader sector trend of senior producers diversifying into base metals at current prices.

headline: US AND JAPAN PLAN WORLD'S DEEPEST UNDERSEA MINE AT 6,000 METRES: Minamitorishima Rare Earth Mud Could Meet Centuries of Demand — Direct Challenge to China
snippet: The US and Japan are advancing joint plans to mine rare earth-bearing mud from 6,000 metres beneath the Pacific Ocean floor near the uninhabited Japanese island of Minamitorishima — a depth no commercial mining project has ever reached — after Japan demonstrated continuous deep-sea pumping feasibility in February 2026. The seabed deposit is estimated to contain enough heavy rare earth material (including terbium and dysprosium critical for permanent magnets) to satisfy centuries of industrial demand. China already holds exploration rights in adjacent blocks through the International Seabed Authority. A joint US-Japan production agreement would restructure North American and European rare earth supply chains away from Chinese dominance, with strategic value measured in defence and technology independence rather than per-tonne economics.

headline: SUREBET NOW 860 METRES WIDE: Goliath GOT Confirms Northeast Expansion, 10.32 g/t Au Over 6m as 50,000-Metre BC Golden Triangle Campaign Reaches Midpoint
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GOT) has expanded the Golden Gate Zone at its Surebet Discovery by an aggregate 860 metres in 2026 — 320 metres northeast (drill hole GD-26-424: 10.32 g/t Au over 6.00m, including 33.80 g/t over 1.82m) plus 540 metres southwest confirmed by earlier 2026 results — on the 100%-owned Golddigger Property in BC's Golden Triangle. Visible gold was encountered in 25 of 45 holes drilled to date across a fully funded 50,000-metre 2026 program, with the zone remaining open at depth and on strike at both ends. The Golden Triangle has produced major discoveries at GT Gold, Seabridge KSM, and Newcrest's Brucejack; systematic expansion of a high-grade zone in this district at gold above $4,400/oz is a material re-rating catalyst.

headline: CHILE CUTS 2026 COPPER OUTPUT FORECAST AGAIN: Cochilco Slashes to 5.27M Tonnes — Second Straight Quarterly Revision as Codelco Misses by 4.8% in June
snippet: Chile's state copper commission Cochilco has revised its 2026 copper production forecast downward for the second consecutive quarter, cutting 300,000 tonnes from the prior estimate to 5.27 million tonnes — a 2.6% decline from 2025 output — citing underperformance at state-owned Codelco and BHP's Escondida and Spence mines. Codelco's June 2026 output alone fell 4.8% to 114,400 metric tonnes. The commission simultaneously raised its 2026 average copper price forecast to US$5.95/lb, acknowledging the US pre-tariff import pull that has diverted metal away from international markets. The structural paradox — the world's largest copper-producing country revising volume down while prices reach multi-year highs — is precisely the environment in which primary copper development projects with domestic North American supply narratives attract the most strategic investor interest.

headline: CATL'S JIANXIAWO MINE RETURNS: Lithium Carbonate Hits 6-Month Low CNY 140,000 as ~46,000t LCE Annual Capacity Rejoins Oversupplied Market
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices fell to CNY 140,000 per tonne in August 2026 — the lowest level in nearly six months — as CATL's Jianxiawo mine resumed operations under a June 29 safety permit, returning nameplate capacity of approximately 100,000 tonnes LCE (net contribution ~46,000 mt LCE, representing 3% of global supply and 8-10% of China's domestic output) to a market already absorbing restarts at MinRes Bald Hill and Core Lithium Finniss in Australia. Higher prices in H1 2026 triggered the wave of mine restarts now dampening the recovery. For junior lithium developers: the near-term equilibrium is being reset lower by returning capacity before EV and grid storage structural demand resumes dominance — the entry thesis is intact but the price deck for project financing needs to reflect current conditions, not H1 peak assumptions.

headline: URANIUM TERM PRICES HIT 18-YEAR HIGH OF $94 WHILE SPOT IDLES AT $87 — Widest Gap in Years Signals Utilities Running Out of Time to Contract
snippet: Uranium's long-term contract price reached $94 per pound in June 2026 — the highest level in 18 years — while the spot market consolidates at $86-87/lb, producing one of the widest term/spot divergences in the sector's history. Analysts attribute the gap to utilities accelerating long-term contracting ahead of the 2028 Russian uranium import ban deadline and AI data centre power demand driving earlier-than-expected nuclear fuel procurement, while spot buyers exercise patience expecting near-term softness. Mine suspensions linked to sulfuric acid shortages and accelerating Chinese reactor approvals are compressing the supply side of term contracts further. Historically, when term/spot divergence reaches this magnitude, spot convergence is upward rather than downward — the direction of resolution has been consistent in every prior uranium cycle.

headline: 103 g/t Au GRAB AT HISTORIC OPHIR-LADE: Silver Pony PONY Returns High-Grade Gold at BC Target — 1,225m Opening Drill Program Complete, Assays Pending
source_name: Rohstoff Welt / Silver Pony Resources Corp. (CSE: PONY)
snippet: Silver Pony Resources Corp. (CSE: PONY) reported August 13 that grab samples from historic Ophir-Lade workings on the Silver Pony Project returned 103 g/t gold and 40 g/t gold — important caveat: grab samples are selective by nature and not representative of broader mineralization. The company also confirmed completion of the first-pass four-hole, 1,225-metre drill campaign across the Black Warrior and Old Gold targets, with assay results pending for the maiden drill program. High-grade grab samples near historic workings establish surface gold credibility that must now be corroborated by drill-hole assays; positive first-pass results would validate the follow-up drill program in a district where proximity to historic underground workings is a reliable geological guide.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER STAGING POWERFUL BREAKOUTS — GoldSeek Sees GDX 6% Surge and Silver's 5.38% Single-Day Spike as Technical Confirmation of New Bull Leg
snippet: GoldSeek's latest technical analysis argues that gold and silver are entering a new bull leg rather than staging a dead-cat bounce, pointing to gold's decisive break above multi-month resistance, silver's 5.38% single-session surge, and the GDX's 6.16% advance as confirmation of a structural sentiment shift in precious metals. The analysis distinguishes this week's move from the false breakouts that characterized Q1 2026 by citing volume expansion on the breakout and confirmation across multiple timeframes. For junior gold and silver miners, technical confirmation that the sector ETF has exited a multi-month compression pattern reduces the downside risk of exploration capital commitments and historically catalyses broadening participation from small-caps.

headline: ANALYSTS CONSENSUS: GOLD MINERS TO OUTPERFORM BULLION — Record Margins, M&A Activity, and Institutional Underweight Create 'Once-in-Cycle' Entry Setup
snippet: Multiple analysts surveyed by the Canadian Mining Report argue gold mining equities are positioned to significantly outperform physical gold in 2026, citing three compounding structural factors: operating margins at historic highs (~$3,000/oz gross profit at current gold prices), P/E multiples compressed to 13-20x versus the 30-50x that characterized prior gold cycles, and institutional fund managers still carrying significant underweight positions in mining after years of sector capital withdrawal. The M&A cycle now underway — as majors deploy record free cash flow to acquire juniors at discounted NAV multiples — is the fourth driver, as acquisition premiums paid to exploration companies reset sector-wide valuation floors upward. The setup is broadly similar to 2002-2004, the last time the sector entered a sustained outperformance phase from a base of record metal prices, compressed multiples, and institutional underweight.

headline: GOLD-STOCK BREAKOUT: REAL OR A HEAD-FAKE? Mining.com Tests Whether the GDX Technical Setup Has Fundamental Support to Hold
snippet: Mining.com's analytical piece examines whether the recent GDX breakout from its February-July 2026 falling wedge is technically sound and fundamentally supported — or whether elevated energy and labour costs, geopolitical risk premium embedded in the gold price, and potential Hormuz de-escalation could reverse the move. The analysis focuses on the distinction between a price-driven rally (where miner margins expand mechanically) and a valuation re-rating (where the market reassigns a higher earnings multiple to the sector) — and argues the current setup qualifies as the latter because Q2 2026 earnings are the first reporting season in which the gold price has been sustainably above $4,000/oz long enough to translate into year-over-year earnings comparisons that make the valuation disconnect undeniable to quantitative investors.
